new_value: The Cajun French Music Association, a nonprofit founded in 1984 to promote and preserve Cajun music, keeps its hall of fame at 240 South C.C. Duson Street, a block from the Liberty Theatre. The museum opened on November 29, 1997, in a one-room country store building from the 1930s, and the first inductees were announced that day; the list now runs past one hundred musicians nominated by the association's chapters. Inside are fiddles, accordions, guitars, hats and belts that belonged to them, some of the earliest Cajun records, and old dance hall advertisements. Many of those honored played on front porches and in small halls before the music was fashionable. Admission is free.
